capabilities.name: Authored scene event
capabilities.summary: Run validated dialogue, rewards, flags, challenges and bounded actor choreography on interaction.

configuration.name: repeatable
configuration.limits: Required explicit value; challenge requires true.

limits: Choreography supports sequential moves, facing, three reaction cues and waits; no parallel groups or custom animation scripts.
Movement is limited to 128 steps and 4096 inspected cells per destination; waits to 5 seconds.
Scene event history is limited to 256 entries.

examples.intent: Run validated dialogue, rewards, flags, challenges and bounded actor choreography on interaction.
examples.usage: Consult dist/src/domain/scenes.js and reuse the existing definition.
examples.expected: Resolve bounded actor actions and commit durable scene results before transient presentation.

evidence.assertion: Regression coverage of the existing contract; this is not a new visual approval.

details.conditions: Optional when condition evaluated through objective conditions.
details.actions: Dialogue, reward, flag, challenge, move, face, wait and react; challenge must be last. See docs/SCENE_ACTIONS.md for choreography limits.
details.rewards: Scene rewards accept coins, potions and orbs, not arbitrary inventory item IDs.
details.repetition: Explicit repeatable boolean; challenge events must be repeatable.
details.persistence: Non-repeatable events use saved map/event keys; rewards and flags commit before choreography and roll back if saving fails.

capabilities.name: Battle potion
capabilities.summary: Consume the configured battle potion in battle to heal the active companion by its pack-defined effect.
limits: Healing is capped at the companion's maximum HP and requires an available mapped supply.
Does not increase player speed or confer a three-battle buff.

examples.intent: Consume a potion in battle to apply the selected pack's healing effect.
examples.usage: Consult dist/src/domain/battle.js and reuse the existing definition.
examples.expected: Consume one mapped potion and heal the active companion according to its pack definition.

evidence.assertion: Regression coverage of the existing contract; this is not a new visual approval.

details.contexts: Battle action; no claim of an exploration-use interface.
details.consumption: Consumes one available potion on successful use.
details.strength: Pack-defined effect, capped by maximum HP.
details.stacking: Repeated uses heal again up to max HP; no buff stacking.
details.persistence: Remaining supplies and health use the existing battle/save transaction.

capabilities.name: Structured brief scaffold
capabilities.summary: Compile a brief into an isolated validated candidate pack scaffold.
limits: This does not turn every scene intent into a fully authored playable interaction.

examples.intent: Compile a brief into an isolated validated candidate pack scaffold.
examples.usage: Use the existing contract documented at scripts/compile-brief.mjs.
examples.expected: Compile a brief into an isolated validated candidate pack scaffold.

evidence.assertion: Existing regression evidence for this capability.

details.inputs: Versioned brief and a new outside-repository output directory.
details.sequence: Validate, scaffold, add maps, retain brief, hash files, validate pack, atomically move candidate.
details.results: Candidate-review page and linked maps; prose roles remain review notes.
details.cancellation: No promotion; existing output destination is refused.
details.errors: Invalid briefs, unsafe locations and existing directories fail without replacing the playable pack.
details.persistence: Retained brief and revision are authoring artefacts, not save state.

limits: Structural and diff checks do not prove prose accuracy; scoped exceptions require reviewer assessment.

examples.intent: Generate and validate resource fiches from canonical records and reviewed templates.
examples.usage: Run npm run catalogue:write then npm run catalogue:check.

evidence.assertion: Deterministic generation, source freshness, references and diff-impact failure cases.

details.inputs: Existing registries, audited templates and curated capabilities.
details.sequence: Extract factual records, apply reviewed family descriptions, generate index/fiches/source hashes.
details.results: Portable repository-local text/JSON index; visual browsing/export is a separate later step.

capabilities.name: Elemental combat presentation
capabilities.summary: Show a distinct, type-colored elemental burst when a companion uses its special move.
limits: The burst reuses the optional five-state combat atlas and falls back to the static portrait when a pack has no combat sheet.
It does not change damage, timing, saves or battle outcomes.

examples.intent: Use the companion's elemental move during a battle.
examples.usage: Reuse the existing Element action; the presentation derives its color from the companion type.
examples.expected: The ally uses the elemental motion and a type-colored burst while the enemy receives the normal hit reaction.

evidence.assertion: Battle playback distinguishes Quick strike and Element, and reduced motion pins the elemental presentation to one frame.

details.trigger: A resolved battle action with kind element.
details.inputs: The existing companion type and optional five-state combat atlas.
details.sequence: Render the attack row with a deterministic expanding type-colored burst and the elemental lunge motion.
details.results: The ally's elemental move reads differently from Quick strike while the enemy receives the normal hit reaction.
details.cancellation: The existing animation cancellation replaces the effect when the battle view changes.
details.errors: Packs without combat atlases fall back to the static portrait; unsupported types use the shared green fallback color.
details.persistence: Presentation-only; battle rules and saved outcomes are unchanged.

capabilities.name: Guardian counterplay rewards
capabilities.summary: Show the next guardian action and matchup-based damage, then reward a valid tactical response when the fight is won.
limits: Damage is a random-roll range for the current active companion; switching changes the matchup and forecast.

Bonuses are granted once per qualifying response in one guardian fight; they do not make any single creature mandatory. A response that requires a later enemy action is not credited if the guardian is defeated first.

examples.intent: Read a guardian's next action, compare current and Guard damage, and choose a response before its turn.
examples.usage: Configure counterplay in a tactic under dist/maps/registries.json and use the existing Guard action.
examples.expected: The forecast identifies action order, damage ranges, current Focus or response availability; a qualifying response is named with bonus coins and XP on victory.

evidence.assertion: Damage-range parity with the resolver; brace, repeated-element, charge and heavy timing; response qualification, payout, checkpoint persistence and invalid-ID filtering.
Forecast remains legible in keyboard, touch, reduced-motion and fullscreen browser states.

details.trigger: While a guardian battle is idle, the interface previews its next tactic action and any relevant response window.
details.inputs: The deterministic tactic pattern position, species damage formula, current active matchup, Guard factor, Focus, party health and configured response conditions.
details.sequence: Derive the upcoming action, unguarded and guarded random damage ranges, brace or charge effects and matching responses without mutating battle state. The existing resolver independently records only qualifying player actions and pays recorded bonuses on victory.
details.results: The battle panel explains whether the guardian acts after the player's choice, the current ally's damage range, Guard reduction/riposte, Focus cost, next brace/charge consequence, and any available response reward.
details.cancellation: The forecast is hidden while an action resolves or the battle ends. A lost or abandoned fight pays no response bonus; a saved interrupted fight retains recorded responses. A response requiring the guardian's next action is not recorded if the player's action defeats it first.
details.errors: Unknown response IDs in a saved battle are discarded during normalization.
details.persistence: The forecast is derived and adds no save fields. Recorded response IDs remain part of the existing battle checkpoint and compatible with older saves.

capabilities.name: Scene choreography
capabilities.summary: Stage bounded actor movement, facing, reactions and waits before dialogue.
limits: Sequential player and ranger movement only; no parallel groups or custom animation scripts.
Each destination is limited to 128 steps and 4096 inspected cells; waits are at most 5 seconds.

examples.intent: Stage two actors approaching and facing before a conversation.
examples.usage: Consult docs/SCENE_ACTIONS.md and validate the event against the map.
examples.expected: Supported moves complete, report blocked/cancelled explicitly, then show dialogue when the UI remains available.

evidence.assertion: Covers bounded routes, walkable destinations, actor validation and explicit arrival/block results.

details.inputs: Player and ranger landmark IDs, integer walkable destinations, supported face targets, notice/surprise/happy reactions, and bounded waits.
details.sequence: Actions run in authored order; each movement settles before the next action.
details.results: Movement reports arrived, blocked or cancelled. Player directions and four ranger facings use shipped sprite poses.
details.cancellation: Pause, menu, map travel, battle, hidden tab and page exit release movement ownership and cancel timers.
details.errors: Missing actor, invalid destination, blocked route or unsupported action is rejected or reported; no rescue teleport is used.
details.persistence: One-time event keys, flags and rewards save before presentation; a failed save restores the prior save state.
